summary: Defines an option in IPv6 Router Advertisement messages that expands the number of flag bits available. The original 8-bit flags field in Neighbor Discovery was close to being used up by various protocols. This option adds room for more flags. It is a standards-track specification and replaces RFC 5075.

eli5.summary: A form has only eight little checkboxes and they are almost all used. This adds a second sheet with many more checkboxes.

questions: what are the ra flag bits
what is the ipv6 ra flags option
how many flag bits does the expanded flags option add
subtitle: A new Router Advertisement option that adds 48 more flag bits when the original 8-bit flags field ran short.

tldr.problem: The Router Advertisement message in IPv6 Neighbor Discovery has only an 8-bit flags field, and several protocols had claimed flags or were about to claim enough to use it up.
tldr.mechanism: The Expanded Flags Option (Type 26) is appended to a Router Advertisement and carries additional flag bits, numbered 8 to 55, with strict rules for senders and receivers.
tldr.outcome: RFC 5175 obsoletes RFC 5075 and gives new protocols room to define flags, with a new IANA registry for them.

today: RFC 5175 is a Proposed Standard and, per the unit metadata, no later RFC obsoletes or updates it. It obsoletes RFC 5075.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
The Router Advertisement (RA) message in the IPv6 Neighbor Discovery Protocol (NDP), defined in RFC 4861, has an 8-bit field reserved for single-bit flags. Several protocols have reserved flags there, and others are preparing to reserve enough to exhaust it.

RFC 5175 defines an option for the RA message that adds 48 more flag bits. The RFC notes that other protocols in the works, such as Detecting Network Attachment, want flags in NDP messages.
sections.eli5: Routers announce themselves with a note that has a few yes/no boxes. The boxes were almost full, so this paper adds more.

sections.title: The Existing Router Advertisement Flags
sections.content:
The RA header flags defined in published RFCs are: M, the Managed Address Configuration flag; O, the Other Configuration flag; H, the Mobile IPv6 Home Agent flag; Prf, the two-bit Router Selection Preferences; and P, the Neighbor Discovery Proxy flag. The last two bits are reserved.

With more protocols wanting flags, the RFC concludes that an expansion capability is needed.
sections.eli5: Each box already has a job, like "ask the server for your address" or "I am a home helper". Only two boxes were left empty.

sections.title: The Expanded Flags Option
sections.content:
NDP lets new options be defined, and RFC 5175 uses that to define the Expanded Flags Option (EFO). Its Type is 26. The Length MUST be checked when processing so the option can grow later. An implementation of this specification MUST set the Length to 1, MUST ignore unrecognized data, and MUST be able to recognize the specific length so it can skip over unrecognized bits.

The remaining bits are allocated by IANA, and their meaning is defined in the document that requests the allocation. They are numbered from left to right, from 8 to 55, starting at bit offset 16 in the option, continuing the numbering of the flags in the RA header. Bits 0 to 7 stay in the RA message header.
sections.eli5: The extra sheet has a label and a size, then a row of new checkboxes. Which box means what is decided later by whoever asks for it.

sections.title: Sending and Receiving Rules
sections.content:
When sending, the option MUST occur only in Router Advertisement messages, MUST occur before any options associated with flags it sets, MUST occur only once per message, and MUST NOT be added if no flags in it are set. All unused flags MUST be zero.

When receiving, a node MUST ignore the option in any message other than an RA, MUST ignore every instance except the first, MUST ignore it if the Length is less than 1, and MUST ignore any unknown flag bits.
sections.eli5: Use the extra sheet only in router announcements, only once, and only if you ticked a box. If you do not understand a box, just skip it.

sections.title: IANA Considerations
sections.content:
IANA defined IPv6 Neighbor Discovery option type 26, "RA Flags Extension Option", and created a registry of IPv6 ND Router Advertisement flags covering both the RA header flags and the extension option. In that registry, bits 0 to 5 are the existing flags, bits 6 to 53 are available for assignment, and bits 54 and 55 are for private experimentation.

Assigning new RA flags, in either the RA header or this option, requires standards action or IESG approval.
sections.eli5: A keeper of the official list hands out the new checkboxes, and only after careful approval. Two boxes at the end are left for people to try things out.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The option shares the security issues of NDP, documented in the Security Considerations of RFC 4861. The RFC adds that extra optional bit fields provide a potential covert channel that is useful for passing information.
sections.eli5: Extra boxes could be used to pass secret notes, so keep that in mind.

fields.name: Length
fields.desc: Senders of this specification MUST set it to 1.
